row.evidence: Buildkite's pricing page lists "SCIM, custom SAML & ADFS" only on the Enterprise plan (Custom, Contact sales), and the Okta guide says "Buildkite customers on the Enterprise plan can optionally enable automatic deprovisioning for their Buildkite users."
row.notes: New row. SSO (Okta, OneLogin, GitHub, Google Workspace OpenID) starts on Pro ($30 per active user/month; the pricing page shows no annual/monthly toggle, so billing basis is unstated); Entra ID, custom SAML, ADFS and SCIM are Enterprise-only, and Enterprise carries a 30 user minimum. SCIM is deprovisioning-focused: an IdP SCIM create only makes a lightweight tracking record, the real account is created by JIT at first SSO login, and SCIM deactivation removes the user from the organization (their personal Buildkite account is untouched). Documented for Okta (OIN app) and Entra (non-gallery app); custom SAML needs a support-enabled 'SCIM for Custom SAML' flag. Group sync is turned off in the Entra setup; team mapping happens through the SAML 'teams' attribute. The REST API (members, invitations, teams) is documented with no plan gate; the audit events API is Enterprise-only.

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Up to 50 users. SSO with Okta, OneLogin, GitHub and Google Workspace (OpenID); no annual/monthly toggle on the pricing page.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: 30 user minimum. Adds SCIM, custom SAML, ADFS, Entra ID SSO and the audit log.

auth.token_source: Organization Settings > Single Sign On > the SSO provider's settings (Base URL and API Token)
auth.notes: The docs call it an API Token; Entra takes it as the Secret Token. Method is recorded as bearer because Okta/Entra send it as a bearer token; the SCIM base URL pattern is not published (shown per provider in settings).

endpoints.notes: No SCIM API reference is published; only user create and deactivate are documented.

operations.notes: SCIM create only makes a tracking record (name, email, active); the account and org membership are created by JIT at first SSO login.

deprovision.data_retained: The user is removed from the Buildkite organization; their personal Buildkite account and other organization memberships are not affected.

attributes.notes: From the Entra mapping instructions (keep exactly these four mappings); the Okta guide says the tracking record stores name, email and active status.

roles.how: Not via SCIM. Admin flag and team membership/role (member or maintainer) are set from SAML attributes (admin, teams) at login.

limitations.text: SCIM create does not create a Buildkite account or org membership; JIT at first SSO login does.
Users created by JIT before SCIM was configured have no SCIM record and cannot be deactivated until re-synced from Okta.
SCIM for custom SAML providers needs a feature flag enabled by Buildkite support.
Entra group provisioning must be disabled.

auth.notes: API access tokens sent as Bearer; GraphQL API also available.

capabilities.notes: Users join by invitation (or JIT); delete_user = remove the member from the organization. Update covers role (admin/member) and sso_mode only.

endpoints.purpose: Update a member's role or SSO mode

rate_limits.text: Default 200 REST requests per minute per organization and 50 per user; GraphQL 20,000 complexity points per 5 minutes per organization.

limitations.text: No API endpoint creates a user directly; members are added by invitation or SSO JIT.

entra.notes: Set up as a non-gallery enterprise app with custom SAML and generic SCIM; no Microsoft Learn tutorial found.

google.notes: Google Workspace SSO via OpenID (Pro) or SAML (Enterprise); no provisioning documented.

onelogin.notes: Buildkite's OneLogin guide covers SSO only.

fallbacks.other_sync: SAML 'teams' attribute maps IdP groups to Buildkite teams at login

open_questions: SCIM base URL pattern, endpoint list (Groups, ServiceProviderConfig) and token expiry are not published.
Whether SCIM update (attribute changes) is supported is not documented; only create and deactivate are listed.
Docs do not say whether a deprovisioned user stops counting as an active user immediately or ends existing sessions.
No user-event webhooks found; JumpCloud catalogue not checked.
The REST members API has no plan gate stated; Free-plan availability is inferred from the per-plan limits page.
